text:
Logan Stanley's season on Long Island has been about size and minutes. The 6-foot-7 defenseman, a Jet for 261 games before brief stops in Buffalo and now the Islanders, is playing almost 21 minutes a night. He missed his Nov. 20 return to Winnipeg, then came back after a two-game absence, as The Hockey News reported.

The scoresheet has been blank. He has five assists in 22 games and no points in his last twelve. Our numbers lean due, at least on the team side: the Islanders are generating about as many chances as usual with him on the ice, and they take 55% of the 5v5 expected goals in his minutes, five points better than without him. His shot clocks in the 99th percentile for top speed, but he uses it rarely, with 15 shots all season and no goals.

Be realistic about the ceiling. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found nothing far from a typical defenseman. He blocks shots (39) and hits (34), and that is the job. The drought says more about bounces than about him.
headline: Logan Stanley, big minutes and an empty column
